html:
Cartagena de Indias is a port city on the Caribbean coast of Colombia, founded by Pedro de Heredia on 1 June 1533. It became one of the most important ports of the Spanish empire.

Gold and silver from the Andes left from Cartagena on the treasure fleets, and it was one of the few ports allowed to receive enslaved Africans for all of Spanish South America. Pirates and enemy fleets attacked it, among them Francis Drake in 1586, so Spain built massive walls and the fortress of San Felipe. The walls held in the great siege of 1741.

The city held a tribunal of the Inquisition and was the base of the saint Peter Claver. Its walled old town became a World Heritage Site in 1984 and is the best-known image of colonial Colombia.
sum: Cartagena de Indias is a port city on the Caribbean coast of Colombia, founded by Pedro de Heredia on 1 June 1533. It became one of the most important ports of the Spanish empire.
